content: Certain glucose-lowering medications exhibit direct protective effects on the kidneys that extend beyond their ability to control blood sugar levels. This mechanism helps slow the rate of glomerular filtration rate (GFR) decline. Additionally, SGLT2 inhibitors mitigate oxidative stress and inflammation within kidney tissues, further contributing to renal protection. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists also provide protective effects for the kidneys. However, the renoprotective mechanisms and benefits of GLP-1 receptor agonists are not as extensively studied or understood as those of SGLT2 inhibitors. When selecting glucose-lowering therapies for patients, particularly those with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD), it is essential to consider the dual benefits these medications offer for both cardiovascular and renal health.
